analyst_view.overall: A Monday-night relegation derby of the Valencian region: Levante (17th, 11 pts, no win in three) host Elche (18th, 10 pts), one point behind and in the drop zone after defeats to Valencia and Betis, and without a win at the Ciutat de València since 1993. Luís Castro's Levante have no injuries or suspensions; Manu Sánchez is back from a hamstring problem and Ryan and Iván Romero are expected to be available. Anselmi's Elche get Gonzalo Villar, Sangaré and Lemar back in training (Lemar still awaits medical clearance), but Marc Aguado, Houary (in the numbers) and Yago de Santiago stay out, and Revivo and Cepeda are just back from international duty. The numbers do not flag this as a derby and no referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already high for two bottom-four sides, because Levante concede a lot at home and Elche create plenty. A tense six-pointer could make both sides careful, but Elche getting Villar and probably Lemar back adds some craft their recent form lacked. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's. Anselmi's Elche keep the ball and cross a lot for Fer Niño, which the numbers already see in their 31 corners in six games, while Levante have won fewer than expected lately. Nothing new in the team news changes that, so I keep 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, low because Levante have been booked little lately (11 in six). This is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between two sides a point apart, which the numbers do not flag, and Elche's players call it close to a must-win; games like that usually bring more fouls and bookings. No referee is named yet, so a clear but moderate lean up to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting (Levante conceded 103 in six games). Elche's possession game and Levante's leaky home record keep it high, but a nervy six-pointer could also slow it down. Nothing in the news points clearly either way, so I keep 29.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Brugué and Fer Niño, each side's top scorer, are both fit, and Elche's midfield returns (Villar, Lemar) help them build but they have admitted their finishing is short. I keep 8.9.
